messages:
maria: CI started failing for the paged-flash test matrix in the bazel container on main branch this morning. cc: eng-runtime.
ci-bot: build failed: //runtime/attention:flash_paged_test (exit code 1)
jon: posting error snippet below, looks like a glibc symbol issue when linking the native flash kernels.
jon: ```
/usr/bin/ld: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6: undefined reference to `__cxa_thread_atexit_impl'
/usr/bin/ld: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.34' not found (required by /workspace/_bazel/.../external/cuda/libcudart.so)
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
kevin: hmm, we changed base image to ubuntu:20.04 vs 22.04 in the bazel container last week for image size. cuda runtime in our environment expects GLIBC_2.34+.
anya: I also saw some runtime failures locally where the paged-attention test segfaults when the kv-cache grows beyond 4k tokens. Could be two separate issues but they appeared after the same image bump.
sam: repro steps I used: `docker run --rm -it redwood/bazel-ci:latest bash -lc 'bazel test //runtime/... -c opt --test_output=errors'` got the same link error.
rachel: can we pin manylinux-style musl or switch to ubuntu:22.04 image? The container toolchain (gcc 9) + glibc mismatch likely.
maria: proposal: revert base image to 22.04 in CI, and separately open a task to make our flash kernels compatible with older glibc if feasible. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
kevin: reverting is fastest fix for CI. Long term we should vendor a matching libc for the CUDA libs or use the CUDA toolkit pinned image.
jon: also saw warnings about -fPIC vs shared objects. The flashattn compile uses `-fno-common` and the build rule doesn't set `-fPIC` for object files in some configurations. That can bite when linking into a shared `.so`.
anya: stack from the segfault (kv cache):
```
#0 0x7f8c2c1dbfa0 in memcpy
#1 runtime::kv_cache::extend
#2 runtime::attention::paged_forward
#3 runtime::tests::flash_paged_test
```
kevin: suggests an ABI or allocator mismatch at memory-copy time — mixing libstdc++/libc from different toolchains can corrupt malloc/free behavior.
sam: actionable plan: (1) pin CI container to ubuntu:22.04-cc (2) add sanity check in CI to compare `ldd --version` and `g++ --version` across matrix configs (3) add an integration job that runs the paged-attention stress test with varied kv sizes.
maria: assigning kevin to 1, jon to 2, anya to 3. Please confirm.
kevin: confirmed, I'll revert the image in the CI job and push a hotfix.
jon: I'll add a small bazel shard that runs `ldd --version` and `readelf -s` on the built .so to catch symbol mismatches early.
anya: I'll create the stress harness for kv cache and add it to flakes so it runs weekly.
rachel: small note: when rebuilding flash variants, ensure we define D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI consistently across compile units — mixing 0/1 will look fine but crash at runtime.
kevin: noted, will add a toolchain flag in bazelrc: `cxx_builtin_include_directory` and `--cxxopt=-D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1`.
maria: CI hotfix ETA?
kevin: will cut a PR in ~30m. If tests pass I'll merge and restart failing jobs.
ci-bot: PR opened: #2892 - revert ci/base-image to ubuntu:22.04. CI: pending.
jon: follow-up: we should also audit any prebuilt libs we bring in (third_party/flash_kernels) — many are built against newer libc versions. Long-term we should publish our own wheels/binaries built in the same CI image.
anya: agreed. I'll add an item to infra backlog: "rebuild prebuilt native kernels in CI image to avoid libc mismatch."
maria: thanks all. If the revert doesn't clear the paged-attention failures, we'll bisect further. :thumbsup:
kevin: update: after image revert PR merged, one of the flaky paged tests still fails locally under ASAN, filing an issue for possible memory overwrite in paged attention code.
jon: tagging @rachel for memory-safety review on paged attention assembly paths.
rachel: I'll take a look tomorrow, could be memcpy size calc when a trailing partial page is handled.
ci-bot: CI rerun: build //runtime/attention:flash_paged_test — PASSED on ubuntu:22.04 image.
maria: great, leaving the stress harness and the prebuilt-rebuild tasks as follow-ups. Closing thread unless new regressions crop up.
